clue.text: Element in deal is sometimes flexible

indicators.note: Element in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some part of a business deal can occasionally bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and supple, able to bend easily.

clue.text: Very active chap,51,composing review

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: composing means putting the letters of the following word together in a new order

explanation.surface: An energetic man writes a critical review.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral 51 is a Roman number here; 'composing' is the anagram signal, not a writer at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an energetic, lively person full of go.

clue.text: Rigorous Australian restricting good conservationists

indicators.note: restricting means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Strine is a jocular name for Australian English
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A strict Australian keeps the green campaigners in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' signals a container. The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and exacting, as stringent rules or standards are.

clue.text: Poet lifted timeless piece of turf

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the remaining letters are read upwards
timeless asks for the letter T, the abbreviation for time, to be taken out

parts.note: a divot is a chunk of turf cut out, as by a golf club

explanation.surface: A poet picked up an ageless lump of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping T (time) from DIVOT leaves DIVO, and 'lifted' turns it upwards to give the Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman author of the Metamorphoses, a classic example of a poet.

clue.text: Pig in fat and port once

indicators.note: in means the pig word sits inside the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A pig in fat makes an old-fashioned seafaring scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port once' tells you the word is obsolete; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The old nautical name for the left-hand side of a ship, later replaced to avoid confusion with starboard.

clue.text: Cordial Ulster group tucking into cooked tea

indicators.note: tucking into means placing one piece inside another
cooked means the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: NI stands for Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A Belfast party sits down to a meal of brewed tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns TEA into ATE, and 'tucking into' puts NISET inside it: A-NISET-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured liqueur, a cordial being a sweet alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Hobby from which one must get a big buzz?

definitions.text: Hobby from which one must get a big buzz?

parts.words: Hobby from which one must get a big buzz?
parts.note: a big buzz sounds like thrills, but here it is the literal hum of a hive of insects

explanation.surface: A pastime that offers great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping hives of honey-making insects is a pastime that literally fills one's ears with humming.

clue.text: Tact I deployed in room

indicators.note: deployed means the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomacy used in a chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A room just under the roof of a house.

clue.text: Diamonds before time found at great cost

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Jewels bought ahead of schedule came expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay dearly is to pay a high price.

clue.text: Unfriendly canine on mound

parts.note: C is the dental notation for a canine tooth
a hill is a raised mound of earth

explanation.surface: A hostile dog stands on a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a dog, but here it is the tooth, marked C on dental charts; 'on' places it before HILL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldness in manner, as in a chill reception, is a lack of warmth.

clue.text: Virginia is beginning to hanker after navy coat

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
RN is the Royal Navy
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An American state yearns to follow the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of varnish is a glossy protective layer painted on.

clue.text: Sluggishness at home I rate peculiar

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: peculiar means the letters are set in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone lounging about the house rates their own laziness as strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency to stay still and do nothing; inactivity.

clue.text: Sack, perhaps, producing complaint, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the complaint is said out loud to give the answer

parts.note: a whine is a moaning complaint

explanation.surface: A bag produces a grumble, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack is an old name for a dry sherry, as drunk by Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack, a fortified white drink from Spain, is an example of an alcoholic grape drink.

clue.text: Correct line club broadcast about exercise

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the other piece
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A club's gym session is aired on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns LINE CLUB into BLUENCIL, and 'about' puts PE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit or censor text, from the coloured pencil traditionally used by editors.

clue.text: Man MEP hires corruptly in large part of world

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: corruptly means the letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A Member of the European Parliament takes staff on dishonestly across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not part of the anagram: it gives a pronoun, and only 'MEP hires' is shuffled by 'corruptly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of the globe, such as the northern or western half.

clue.text: Turn for information about English joint

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to refer is to turn to a source for information

explanation.surface: Consult the reference books about an English pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Second gratuity appearing before complete pay

indicators.note: appearing before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity
to end something is to complete it

explanation.surface: Some extra cash from a tip shows up before the full wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular salary, as paid to a clergyman.

clue.text: Basis for writing about mediocre entertainment school promoted

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means the whole sequence is read upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
pap is bland, worthless entertainment
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: Notes about a dull show put on at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns RE + PAP + ETON upside down in this down clue; Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper for letters is the medium on which one writes.

clue.text: Attractive publication with new name backed

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication

indicators.note: backed means the word is written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name

explanation.surface: A magazine with a new title went into reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing things towards itself, as a lodestone does, or charming.

clue.text: Dashing hero's tag showing deficiency

explanation.surface: A handsome champion's label reveals a flaw.

clue.text: Decent tale spread about this Roman

spread means the letters are spread out in a new arrangement

parts.note: hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A story is told of this upstanding Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' gives ETAL, and 'about' wraps it round the Latin word, since Latin was the Romans' language.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally right and proper.

clue.text: I sing appearing as fool in school

indicators.note: in means the fool word sits inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: nit is short for nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: A dunce appears at school to perform a song.

explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang verbs for informing on someone to the authorities.

clue.text: Not all notice captured area that's frozen out

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: One obliged to serve ambassador with fortune

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

clue.text: Creature in accord about much of old military hardware

parts.note: to chime is to agree or be in accord

clue.text: Bay tree's top seen below hazy line

explanation.walkthrough: 'hazy' turns LINE into INLE, and the first letter of 'tree's' goes under it.

clue.text: Galvanise help for rider

explanation.surface: Rouse the aid for a horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur is to urge into action; a spur is a spiked device on a horseman's heel used to urge the mount on.

clue.text: Reported source of stories has instrument

parts.note: a liar is someone who tells tall stories

clue.text: Retired priest entertained by highly fashionable channel

parts.note: cult as in cult following, wildly popular

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' gives VER, and 'entertained by' is the container signal; 'channel' here is a watercourse, not television.

clue.text: Greek area producing old play? I'm excited!

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.definitionFit: The sanctuary in the Peloponnese where the ancient Games were held.

clue.text: Quality shown when enduring game

explanation.surface: A virtue displayed while putting up with a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm forbearance under trouble; also the solitaire card game.

clue.text: Rank tailless bird within borders of Derbyshire

explanation.definitionFit: A level or grade on a scale of status.
